A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReTeX work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReTeX experiments on vision and NLP tasks, including benchmark results, unseen-task evaluations, robustness tests, ablations, and seed statistics.

after.justification: v2 retains original ReTeX experimental results in Tables 1–5 and Appendices D–F, including larger vision suites, corruption tests, ablations, and five-seed measurements.

M1.justification: SVD-based task identification, parameter-supervised low-rank offset recovery, ReTeX-E, Dirichlet-based soft recovery, and grouped inference remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 8/14/20/30/50-task vision suites, seven NLP tasks, fine-grained bird tasks, unseen-task scenarios, and input corruptions (Section 5 and Appendix D).

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in corresponding experiments, including ID-LoRA and ID-EMR-Merging in Table 5 and AdaMerging/WEMoE in Table G. The expanded SiM discussion adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The backbones, task splits, metrics, 5,000-iteration recovery training, default 64 reference inputs per task, and grouped inference with B = 64 are retained. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The rank, embedding, reference-set, representation-source, loss, factorization, and layer-sharing ablations are retained. Corruption tests, interpolation comparisons, and the WSC prediction-flip analysis also already appear in v1.

E5.justification: Appendix E.4 and Table H retain the same five seeds, numbered 0–4, and the same mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for 8/14/20 tasks. No uncertainty-reporting procedure or run count changes.

E6.justification: Matched Tables 1–5 and B–I and the result figures retain their numerical values and findings. For example, Table 4 still reports ReTeX average accuracy of 86.6 with 97.5% normalized accuracy, and Table E retains 81.5 accuracy on 50 tasks.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, affine-recovery derivation, and Theorems 1–2 with their proofs in Appendix A are unchanged. The altered equation cross-reference in A.2 does not change the formulas or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-checkpoint expert recovery, router-free task identification, plug-and-play application, and unseen-task generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of recovery, soft interpolation, scalability, and WSC sensitivity remain unchanged. Appendix G retains the limitations concerning additional recovery training and dependence on reference inputs.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, pseudocode, module parameterization, hyperparameters, GPU specifications, training time, and code-access statement remain unchanged. Added bibliography access dates do not alter resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 explicitly connects ReTeX to SiM's SVD-based task signals and distinguishes conditioning expert recovery from selecting stored components. It also expands discussion of HyperNetworks, FiLM, and CNAPs, already covered in Appendix B. The cited-work set is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 receives limited rewriting, the affiliation gains a country, and several references gain access dates; the section hierarchy is retained. Appendix A.2 incorrectly changes its offset-only-rule reference from Eq. (5) to Eq. (4).

P2.justification: Existing displays are enlarged, particularly Table 2 and Figures 1–2. Running headers and page numbers are added, and figures, tables, and algorithms are repositioned through reflow. The display inventory and plotted content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Larger key displays, especially Table 2 and Figure 2, improve legibility, while Section 2 more explicitly explains the relationship to SiM. These modest presentation and positioning gains outweigh the small regression from Appendix A.2's incorrect Eq. (4) reference. The scientific methods and evidence remain unchanged.
